A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaOptimize research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet-18 experiments on CIFAR10 and ImageNet and language-model training results on TinyStories.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds optimizer comparisons and measured runtime and GPU-space overheads.

M1.justification: The framework and approximation choices remain intact, but Algorithms 2–3 revise printed update rules. Algorithm 3 changes the Lion meta-step multiplier from alpha_t to eta and restores momentum weighting consistent with the existing Appendix A formulas. These are local procedural corrections, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10 and ImageNet image classification and TinyStories language modeling. Additional optimizer configurations and computational measurements use the retained datasets and tasks; no new domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 adds DoG, gdtuo, Prodigy, and mechanic to the ImageNet and TinyStories comparisons, alongside the retained fixed-step-size and cosine-schedule baselines. ImageNet's DoG learning curve is explicitly omitted for poor performance, but its evaluation and overhead results are reported. CIFAR10's comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a separate computational evaluation using relative per-iteration runtime and maximum-feasible-batch-size ratios for GPU-space overhead. Appendix C specifies tuning and selection procedures for the added baselines, including matched initial step sizes for gdtuo and mechanic. Figure 4 also adds an ImageNet (SGDm, Lion) configuration; the original learning-curve settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Initial-step-size sensitivity and blockwise step-size analyses in Figures 2–3 are retained. The ImageNet scalar-versus-blockwise comparison in v1 Figure 4 reappears in v3 Appendix D, Figure 6. The new comparator and cost benchmarks do not introduce a new targeted ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. DoG's newly documented polynomial averaging concerns optimizer iterates, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 add learning curves for the new comparators, and Figure 4 adds (SGDm, Lion). New Table 1 reports MetaOptimize (AdamW, Lion) overheads of 44% time and 33% space on ImageNet, and 13% time and 0% space on TinyStories. The retained TinyStories finding that the tuned cosine schedule performs better remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the scalar recurrence's initial condition Y_0 from 0 to 1 and replaces the H-update coefficient gamma Y_t + (1-gamma) with Y_t. This is a limited mathematical revision. The discounted objective, general derivation, and special-case arguments in Appendices A–B remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces its empirical contribution about competing with manually designed schedules with a claim of outperforming state-of-the-art automatic hyperparameter optimization methods across CIFAR10, ImageNet, and language modeling. The abstract's schedule-competitiveness claim and the principal framework and generality contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly qualifies measured overheads by explaining that MetaOptimize's implementation is not optimized for time or space, and identifies DoG's sensitivity to initial movement despite its parameter-free designation. Section 9's substantive limitations remain unchanged. Section 5 drops the explicit assertion linking hypergradient descent's short horizon to inferior performance.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds baseline tuning details, implementation provenance, and profiling instructions, and specifies CPU counts. Algorithm 3 explicitly documents SGDm, already used in v1's experiments. The framework's code reference and most original hyperparameter-table entries are retained; these disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying implementations.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to mechanic, D-adaptation, Prodigy, Mahmood et al. (2012), and Javed (2020). Related work now covers distance-adaptation and online-convex-learning approaches and acknowledges additional non-SGD IDBD extensions. The central positioning as a generalization of earlier meta-gradient methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected method and experiment passages are shortened and rewritten, Section 4 is renamed, experiment headings are flattened, and notation conventions move to Appendix A. The generic broader-impact section is removed. The overall narrative sequence and most appendix exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, algorithms are reformatted, and Figures 1–3 become much smaller adjacent displays. Figures 4–5 receive expanded legends and revised axes. The blockwise ImageNet curves move into a separate appendix figure, and a new computational-overhead table reorganizes the results presentation.

improvement.justification: The added automatic-optimizer comparisons and documented time/memory measurements make the practical competitiveness of MetaOptimize better supported than in v1 (Figures 4–5, Table 1, Appendix C). The benefit is tempered by less legible plots and an introduction claim extending superiority to CIFAR10, where Figure 1 still compares only fixed-step-size baselines. Overall, the empirical case improves, while its scope and reporting remain imperfect.
